live.instructions: Aniva: read-only access to the signed-in user's health data (biomarkers, biological age, action plan, supplements, appointments, test sessions, subscription, referrals). Pick the dedicated tool for each topic. Use aniva_get_app_links before suggesting any anivahealth.com URL — every data tool also embeds canonical actions[] you can forward the user to.

tools.name: aniva_get_biomarkers_snapshot
tools.title: Get biomarkers snapshot (latest results)
tools.description: PREFERRED TOOL for "show me my biomarkers", "what are my latest results?", "any out-of-range markers?", "biomarker overview". Returns the user's biomarkers with latest result, unit, reference ranges, and status (below/within/above normal, optimal). Use this (NOT aniva_get_biomarker_trend) when the user wants the broad picture; use aniva_get_biomarker_trend for one specific biomarker over time. Filters out routine OK allergy/intolerance results by default.

profileId.description: Profile UUID. Optional for OAuth-authenticated requests (injected from access token).

limit.description: Optional max biomarkers to return (after filtering).

includePlannedTests.description: Deprecated: planned tests are never included (ignored).

primaryCategory.description: Optional: only biomarkers whose primary_category matches.

context.description: Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."

tools.name: aniva_get_biomarker_trend
tools.title: Get history (trend) for one biomarker
tools.description: PREFERRED TOOL when the user names a specific biomarker (e.g. "how has my HbA1c changed?", "show vitamin D over time", "ferritin trend"). Returns time-series values + reference ranges for ONE biomarker, plus a sparkline widget. Use aniva_get_biomarkers_snapshot for the broad overview instead.

profileId.description: Profile UUID. Optional for OAuth-authenticated requests (injected from access token).

biomarkerId.description: Biomarker ID. Provide either biomarkerId or biomarkerSlug.

biomarkerSlug.description: Biomarker slug (e.g. "hba1c"). Used when biomarkerId is not supplied.

biomarkerName.description: Free-text biomarker name (e.g. "Vitamin D"). Used as last-resort fallback — case-insensitive contains match against name and synonyms.

tools.name: aniva_get_user_metadata
tools.title: Get user metadata (low-level field-level read)
tools.description: Low-level metadata fetcher with field-level selection. PREFER the dedicated tool when one exists: aniva_get_user_summary (name/birthdate/contact), aniva_get_subscription (membership/plan), aniva_get_referrals (referral data + share link). tools.name: aniva_get_supplements
tools.title: Get user supplement plan (active + recommended)
tools.description: PREFERRED TOOL for ANY supplement/vitamin/protocol question — "what should I take?", "what's my stack?", "do I need to reorder?", "what supplements am I on?". ALWAYS returns BOTH lists: `active` = currently taking (purchased + in intake window), `recommended` = Aniva-suggested but NOT yet purchased. Most Aniva users have items in `recommended` even if `active` is empty — present BOTH to the user. Do not call the `recommended` list "your stack" or "what you're taking"; they're suggestions awaiting purchase. The widget renders both sections automatically.
